1973.notes: Secondary source (Banner-Graphic, Greencastle, Indiana, Associated Press report 'Deadline For Second Tax Phase Is Sunday', June 28, 1973, via Hoosier State Chronicles): the Adams County Council turned down the 1973 local option income tax. The county adjusted gross income tax, Indiana's first county income tax, was enacted in 1973; counties adopting it by June 1, 1973 imposed it from July 1, 1973 (31 counties did), and those adopting by July 1 imposed it from January 1, 1974. So no county income tax in 1973. Single secondary source.

1992.notes: The 'Resident County Tax Rates' chart (columns 1992 to 1996) on page 13 of the Department of Revenue's Form IT-40P booklet for 1996 and earlier tax years (Wayback Machine copy, PDF page 13) prints 'N/A' for this county in 1992, i.e. no county income tax at the resident rate that year.

1993.notes: Resident rate is the combined CAGIT or COIT plus CEDIT rate as printed in the DOR county tax rate chart for the year; the components are not modelled separately. Deduction is the $1,000 per person exemption. 1993 rate from the 'Resident County Tax Rates' chart (columns 1992 to 1996) on page 13 of the Department of Revenue's Form IT-40P booklet for 1996 and earlier tax years (Wayback Machine copy of the Department's prior-year forms page, PDF page 13); the chart gives one calendar-year rate per county, prorated where a county's rate changed during the year.
